claims.text: Rapid-quenched FeCoNiTi forms a dual-phase microstructure containing an fcc solid solution and a hexagonal C14 Laves phase.
The FeCoNiTi system exhibits ferromagnetic ordering transitions near 1084 K, 214 K, and 168 K.
Coexistence of the C14 Laves phase significantly enhances the coercivity of FeCoNiTi.
The C14 phase is Ti-rich, whereas the fcc matrix is enriched in Fe, Co, and Ni.
Strong antiferromagnetic coupling develops between the Ti-rich C14 sublattice and the Fe/Co/Ni-rich fcc matrix.
Antiferromagnetic interphase coupling suppresses the net saturation magnetization attributed to the fcc phase.
Introducing nonferromagnetic alloying elements into FeCoNi-based alloys can reduce saturation magnetization.
The fcc–C14 phase boundaries form high-energy pinning sites for magnetic domain walls.
Domain-wall pinning at fcc–C14 boundaries raises the energy barrier for wall motion and thereby increases coercivity.
Ti 3d moments in the C14 structure align antiparallel to the 3d moments of Fe, Co, and Ni in the fcc phase.
The C14 phase acts as an antiferromagnetic sink or source of negative exchange bias.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys have a coercivity cap of approximately 100 Oe.
The approximately 100 Oe coercivity cap in single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys results from insufficient orbital moments and a lack of strong pinning mechanisms.
Dual-phase FeCoNiTi can reach a coercivity of approximately 667 Oe at 400 K.
Dual-phase FeCoNiTi will have lower saturation magnetization than a single-phase fcc FeCoNi alloy.
A nanocrystalline, well-dispersed C14 phase is required for effective magnetic interaction with the fcc matrix.
Large isolated C14 grains or insufficient Ti may prevent the proposed coercivity enhancement.
Spin-polarized DFT using an explicit fcc–C14 interface model can compare the fcc-phase spin density of states at the Fermi level with and without the C14 interface.
A comparison between dual-phase fcc+C14 material and a single-phase fcc control at 400 K can test whether the C14 phase enhances coercivity.
